open_points.subject: public_op:source_folder.read_named_source
open_points.text: Nothing when the name fails condition 1 of A3 rule 5. Otherwise a `SourceRead`: one `SourceFile`, and the bytes that were judged when it is ready.
open_points.question: When condition 1 fails because metadata of the path or a segment cannot be read, does the operation return nothing, producing `NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT`, or return a rejected `SourceFile` because “A file that cannot be read is a rejected `SourceFile`,” producing `UNREADABLE_FILE`?
options: Return nothing and map the failure to `NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT`.
Return `SourceRead` with a rejected `SourceFile` whose reason is `unreadable_file`.
open_points.default_guess: Return nothing and map the failure to `NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT`, following A3 condition 1.

witness.initial: A requested relative name is syntactically valid, but metadata for its last path segment cannot be read.
events: The caller requests delivery of the name.
The required pre-opening metadata read fails.
outcomes: `read_named_source` returns nothing, and delivery answers `failed` with `not_ready_or_absent`.
`read_named_source` returns a rejected `SourceFile`, and delivery answers `failed` with `unreadable_file`.
witness.observer: The calling flow sees a different M06 failure reason.

open_points.subject: model:SourceFile returned by public_op:source_folder.observe_source_files
open_points.text: One `SourceFile` for each reported file, in the walking order of A1, with its source id when it is ready.
open_points.question: Which `SourceFile` field carries the number of bytes actually read to end so that `scan_project_photos` can produce M02.size, and is the separately observed listed size also retained?
options: `SourceFile.size` is the number of bytes read to end, with a separate `listed_size` field for the metadata value.
`SourceFile.size` remains the listed size and a separate `read_size` field carries the byte count.
`SourceFile.size` is overloaded: the byte count after an end-of-file read and the listed size otherwise.
open_points.default_guess: Use the M02 rule directly: overload `SourceFile.size` with the byte count after a complete read and the listed size otherwise.

witness.initial: A regular file is listed as 100 bytes and grows to 120 bytes before its single read reaches end of file.
events: It opens the file and reads 120 bytes to end.
outcomes: The returned internal value exposes the completed-read count and M02.size is 120.
The returned internal value exposes only the listed size and M02.size is 100.
witness.observer: The scan caller sees a different M02.size.

open_points.subject: model:SourceRead returned by public_op:source_folder.read_named_source
open_points.text: Otherwise a `SourceRead`: one `SourceFile`, and the bytes that were judged when it is ready.
open_points.question: Where in `SourceRead` or `SourceFile` is the modification time from the one metadata reading of the opened file carried to `photo_delivery`, so that A2 can derive the photo date without another metadata read?
options: Put the opened-file modification time in `SourceFile`.
Put the opened-file modification time in a separate `SourceRead` field.
Return another opened-file metadata value object containing the time.
open_points.default_guess: Put the opened-file modification time in `SourceFile` because it is a fact of the exact file observation represented there.

open_points.subject: imports.module_internal[source_folder]
open_points.text: Otherwise it is read once, up to one byte past the imported `MAX_SOURCE_BYTES` constant
open_points.question: Which provider owns `MAX_SOURCE_BYTES`, and what exact `module_internal[source_folder][provider]` entry authorizes the runtime import required by both source-folder operations?
options: Make `source_folder` the owner of `MAX_SOURCE_BYTES`, so no internal import edge is needed.
open_points.default_guess: Declare it in a configuration/constants provider and list exactly `MAX_SOURCE_BYTES` on the provider edge of `module_internal[source_folder]`.
